subject: Clarify data horizon, derivative artifacts, and deletion path
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightpay.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Questions on default retention horizon & derivative artifacts

Hi Kimberly,

Quick set of questions from our security team as we evaluate Redwood for production:

- What is Redwood's default retention horizon for API requests and responses (prompts vs generated outputs)?
- Do you persist derivative artifacts (embeddings, model traces, KV cache snapshots) by default? If yes, for how long and where are they stored (region)?
- Are customer prompts/outputs ever used to improve models or for training?
- If we submit a deletion request, what is the timeline and what stages does the data go through? Any backup retention windows?

We need a short, precise summary to include in our security questionnaire and a copy of any short retention summary you have.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Security Engineer, BrightPay
elena.morales@brightpay.io

[No attachments]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightpay.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention horizon & derivative artifacts

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Short answers first, then a few bullets with details.

Summary (short):
- Default capture window (hosted API): 60 days for request/response artifacts (includes both prompts and generated outputs).
- Derivatives: embeddings are NOT stored by default unless explicitly requested via the embeddings endpoint with storage enabled; KV cache snapshots used at runtime are ephemeral and not persisted.
- Model training: we DO NOT use customer prompts/outputs to train or fine-tune models by default. Customers may opt in to aggregated telemetry sharing for opt-in programs only.
- Deletion path: a verified deletion request marks records for purge and ordinarily completes within 72 hours for active stores; backup/archival layers (if applicable) are on a rolling 90-day scrub schedule.

Details / nuance:
- "Prompts vs outputs": we treat the full request payload (user prompt + model response) as captured artifacts under the 60-day policy for hosted customers. This is to support debugging, evals, and abuse detection.
- "Derivative artifacts": embeddings and explicit artifact storage are opt-in. We do capture lightweight telemetry (token counts, latency histograms, non-reversible hashes) by default for platform health and billing; those are aggregated and do not contain raw text.
- "KV cache / serving state": runtime caches used to speed inference are transient and not persisted to long-term object storage. Snapshots created for debugging or replay are treated as artifacts and follow the same 60-day window.
- "Residency": by default artifacts are stored in the region tied to the customer's account (US / EU / APAC). We do not replicate across regions unless configured as part of an enterprise contract.
- "Deletion workflow": upon verified deletion request we mark records with a tombstone and remove them from active indexes within 72 hours. A background job purges underlying object storage pointers; physical removal from backups is subject to the backup retention policy (90-day rotation). We provide an audit token once purge completes.

I've attached a short retention summary PDF below (retention_summary_60d_v1.pdf) and included a SOC2 excerpt for the sections customers usually request (SOC2_excerpt.pdf). Also linking our docs: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/data-retention.

If you want, I can also provide an explicit statement we can add to your security questionnaire responses.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: retention_summary_60d_v1.pdf, SOC2_excerpt.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightpay.io>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention horizon & derivative artifacts

Adding a couple of operational points you might find useful for the questionnaire:

- Dedicated / Private customers: retention windows are contract-configurable. If BrightPay prefers "no retention" for requests/outputs we can enable an enterprise profile that does not persist artifacts beyond in-memory serving — this is part of Private/Dedicated terms.
- Canary / Rollout exceptions: any service-level departure from default retention for hosted customers (for example temporary extended capture for a debug window) requires approval from Compliance and Product; those events are logged and timeboxed.
- Model improvement clarifier: we never surface raw customer data into model training pipelines without explicit opt-in. We may use aggregated quality signals (e.g., pass/fail of evals without raw text) to inform platform-level model selection and scheduling.

Happy to draft the exact language for your security questionnaire sections on retention, derivatives, and deletion timelines if that helps.

—Marissa
Lead, Product Security Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightpay.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Thanks Kimberly and Marissa — that's exactly what we needed. Two quick clarifications: 1) the 60-day default applies to both prompts and outputs (confirmed), and 2) backups are on a 90-day scrub (confirmed).

We'll paste a short paragraph from your reply into our security questionnaire and follow up if we need the enterprise "no retention" option. Appreciate the fast responses and the attachments.

Best,
Elena
Security Engineer, BrightPay
